clips.speaker: Grant Liffmann
clips.text: It is devastating. Steph Curry was playing some of the best basketball of his entire career. This guy is 38 years old. They were playing so well, coaching has been on point, the players are responding. Kevon Looney has been great, Kevon Looney has been doing well, and they are doing this all despite not having two presumed stars, definitely one in Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody out as well. So, how about three stars? Chris Paul and Kristaps Porzingis does not exist for that team either. So, they were doing all this, all those vibes are going, and then this happens. This team has shown that even without Steph on the court, they compete. They execute and they play hard.
clips.news_angle: Warriors' resilience and team dynamics without Steph Curry
clips.social_post: Grant Liffmann on the Steph Curry injury: It is devastating. Steph was playing some of the best basketball of his entire career. The Warriors have shown they can compete without him, but losing him is a massive blow to their momentum.
clips.video_title: The Warriors Were Winning—Now Steph Curry Is Hurt | Chris Mannix & Grant Liffmann
clips.pull_quote: This team has shown that even without Steph on the court, they compete.

clips.speaker: Grant Liffmann
clips.text: If they go five and nine and are 500 by the time Steph comes back, you are probably in the play-in world at the bottom of the play-in world at that point, and then you try to make a run at it and Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody come back after that. So, while it is devastating, I actually think they can stay afloat during all this because at the end of the day, I am a firm believer, if you execute and compete, especially on the defensive end, and give everything you got in a regular season game, you have a good shot of winning.
clips.news_angle: Warriors' potential to stay afloat during Steph Curry's absence
clips.social_post: Grant Liffmann believes the Warriors can stay afloat during Steph Curry's absence if they lean on their defense. He says if they can execute and compete, they still have a good shot of winning games.
clips.video_title: The Warriors Were Winning—Now Steph Curry Is Hurt | Chris Mannix & Grant Liffmann
clips.pull_quote: I actually think they can stay afloat during all this.

clips.speaker: Chris Mannix
clips.text: They are going to have to radically change how they play and how they try to win. During this eight-game winning streak they had the best defensive rating in the NBA. They are really going to have to lean into that defense because not only is Steph gone but Brandon Williams is gone as well. So, their backcourt has been decimated by short-term injury. They are really going to have to lean on Draymond Green, who has been outstanding to start the season on that end of the floor. He is going to have to really be a catalyst for this team's success over the next month.
clips.news_angle: Warriors must rely on defense and Draymond Green's leadership
clips.social_post: Chris Mannix says the Warriors must radically change how they play without Steph Curry. He believes they have to lean on their defense and Draymond Green, who has been outstanding to start the season.
clips.video_title: The Warriors Were Winning—Now Steph Curry Is Hurt | Chris Mannix & Grant Liffmann
clips.pull_quote: They are really going to have to lean into that defense.

clips.speaker: Grant Liffmann
clips.text: Draymond Green is an all-time guy. He is not just, you know, we talked about the gravity that Steph Curry brings offensively, the anti-gravity that Draymond Green brings on defense. He is just played free safety, can do so many things, he can dictate how a defense moves. Is he the same defender he was in the past? No, and he cannot bring it every single night and that concerns me a little bit as you go through this because he has to bring it every single night, especially with Steph out.

I mean, I, so how I would call conference contender would be they can win the conference, not in the regular season, win, advance to the finals, basically. Yeah, so no. clips.text: What we're seeing from James Harden, is this permanent or is this a blip? James Harden historically has been a phenomenal regular season player. And when he's slowed down, has often come either in the playoffs for sure, or late in the regular season when all the minutes he plays and all the bumps he takes catches up to him. We're in week three right now of the regular season and James Harden's numbers across the board have been awful. He's I think still sub-40% from the floor, sub-40% from three-point range, scoring numbers are the lowest I think since his rookie year. I mean, all these numbers are like you had to go back to very early Oklahoma City days to see numbers like this from James Harden.

I have never in my life never covered a player that is as good about getting what he wants, both in terms of location and money than James Harden. James Harden gets what James Harden wants. He's got a three-year deal worth nearly $100 million and the back end of that deal is a player option. So you can't convince me, Grant, that when year two is up, he's not going to be able to figure out a way to get like two extra years from the Cavaliers. He can put up 20 a game, but somehow his impact on winning goes away, right? And I think that's what you look for with a James Harden. He may get his numbers back and stuff, and maybe that'll impact winning. Like he has done his entire career. Let's give credit to James Harden. He is one of the best regular season winners ever.
